Cancelling the coroutine cancels the call in the core, and a `Flow` applies backpressure: the runtime grants credit as your collector consumes items. The runtime contains core panics at the boundary, so a bug in the core is a typed failure, not a crash.

## Stores

A store extends `KeelStore`. Every signal is a read-only `StateFlow`; computed signals are updated by the core. Read them in Compose with `collectAsState()`, no extra module needed.

kotlin

```kotlin
class Todos : KeelStore {
    val todos: StateFlow<List<Todo>>
    val filter: StateFlow<Filter>
    val visible: StateFlow<List<Todo>>        // computed by the core
    val remaining: StateFlow<UInt>            // computed by the core

    constructor(ctx: KeelCore = KeelCore.shared)
    fun setFilter(f: Filter)
    suspend fun add(title: String): Todo      // throws TodoError
}
```

kotlin

```kotlin
@Composable
fun TodosScreen(vm: TodosViewModel = viewModel()) {
    val visible by vm.store.visible.collectAsState()
    val remaining by vm.store.remaining.collectAsState()
    Text("$remaining left")
    LazyColumn {
        // the list is keyed by id in the core, so Compose moves and animates rows
        items(visible, key = { it.id }) { todo -> TodoRow(todo) }
    }
}
```

**Hold on to the store.** The runtime's mirror holds a store weakly. A `StateFlow` on its own does not keep the store, and the core object behind it, alive. Keep the store in a `ViewModel` and close it in `onCleared()`.

## Query handles

A `#[keel::query]` becomes a store with five `StateFlow`s (`data`, `status`, `error`, `fetching`, `updatedAt`) plus `refetch()` and `invalidate()`. Constructing it observes the query and fetches when the data is missing or stale.

kotlin

```kotlin
val inbox = RemoteTodosQueryHandle.create("inbox")
val items by inbox.data.collectAsState()        // List<RemoteTodo>?
val busy by inbox.fetching.collectAsState()
```

See [Queries & mutations](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/queries.html).

## Ports

The ten standard ports are implemented in `dev.keel.runtime.adapters` (`OkHttp` or `HttpURLConnection`, `SharedPreferences`-backed files, `EncryptedFile`, `ConnectivityManager`, `ProcessLifecycleOwner` and so on) and are not generated into your module. You replace one by passing an implementation in `LoadOptions.adapters`, keyed by its port id. A port you define yourself becomes an `interface`:

kotlin

```kotlin
interface Http : KeelPort {
    suspend fun request(req: HttpRequest): HttpResponse     // throws HttpError
}
```

See [Ports & adapters](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/ports.html) for the defaults. Android-specific adapters live in the `android-adapters` module, not in the runtime.

## Threading and lifetime

- Signals are updated on `Dispatchers.Main.immediate`, with per-frame coalescing. On a JVM without Android the runtime falls back to a single-thread executor, which is what the JVM test suite uses.
- `KeelStore` and `KeelObject` implement `AutoCloseable`. Call `close()` to release the handle (a `use { }` block works); a `Cleaner` releases leaked handles as a backstop. `KeelCore.stats()` exposes live handle counts.
- Over JNI, callbacks arrive from core threads and are decoded immediately; you never see a raw buffer.

---

Source: https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/api-typescript.html

# API overview, TypeScript

Generated TypeScript is strict-mode ESM with no any in exported types: plain interfaces and unions for data, promises for calls, signals for state, and hooks for React. The core package has no runtime dependencies.

`keel bindgen` writes an npm package (`src/*.ts`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`) that imports only from `@keel/runtime`. The shapes below come from the playground's generated code and the specification (§10.3).

## Loading the core

Load the core once, before you create a store. The runtime compares the core's schema hash with the one the bindings were generated from and rejects a mismatch with `KeelSchemaMismatch`.

web/src/keel.ts

```ts
import { KeelCore } from "@keel/runtime";
import { KeelIds, Todos } from "@playground/core";
import wasmUrl from "../../build/web/keel_core.wasm?url";

await KeelCore.load({
  mode: "wasm-main",                       // the core runs in a wasm module on this thread
  wasm: new URL(wasmUrl, location.href),
  expectedSchemaHash: KeelIds.schemaHash,
  adapters: { http, kv },                  // optional: replace a default adapter
});

const todos = await Todos.create();        // uses KeelCore.shared
```

| `mode` | Where the core runs |
| --- | --- |
| `"wasm-main"` | a wasm module on the page's main thread |
| `"wasm-worker"` | the same module in a worker, keeping the main thread free |
| `"remote"` | the core that `keel dev` serves, over a WebSocket: `{ mode: "remote", url: "ws://127.0.0.1:7443", expectedSchemaHash }` |

## Type mapping

| Rust | TypeScript |
| --- | --- |
| `bool` | `boolean` |
| `i8` … `i32`, `u8` … `u32`, `f32`, `f64` | `number` |
| `i64`, `u64` | `bigint` (or `number` with `#[keel(js_number)]` / `ts_js_number`) |
| `String`, `Bytes` | `string`, `Uint8Array` |
| `Duration`, `Timestamp`, `Uuid` | `Duration`, `Timestamp`, `string` |
| `Option<T>`, `Vec<T>` | `T \| null`, `T[]` |
| `Map<K, V>` | `Map<K, V>` |
| record | `interface` |
| unit enum, data enum | string-literal union, discriminated union on `kind` |
| error | a class extending `KeelError`, with subclasses per variant |

64-bit integers become `bigint` so no value is ever silently rounded; a 64-bit value outside the safe range is a decode error rather than a wrong number when you opt into `number`.

## Records and enums

ts

```ts
/** One item of the to-do list. */
export interface Todo { id: string; title: string; done: boolean }

export type Filter = "all" | "active" | "done";

export type Figure =
  | { kind: "circle"; radius: number }
  | { kind: "rect"; width: number; height: number }
  | { kind: "label"; value: string }
  | { kind: "empty" };
```

A `switch (figure.kind)` over the union is exhaustive under `strict`, so adding a variant in Rust breaks every `switch` that forgot it.

## Errors

A `#[keel::error]` becomes an abstract class with a `kind` and one subclass per variant, so you can branch with `instanceof` or on `kind`. A rejected call carries the typed error, not a string to parse.

ts

```ts
export abstract class TodoError extends KeelError {
  readonly kind: "emptyTitle";
}
export namespace TodoError {
  export class EmptyTitle extends TodoError { /* message: "the title cannot be empty" */ }
}

try {
  await todos.add(draft);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TodoError) setProblem(error.message);
}
```

## Objects and functions

An object is a class holding a handle. **Every method returns a `Promise`**, which keeps the API uniform across main-thread, worker and remote modes. Stream methods return an `AsyncIterable`, and any call takes an optional `AbortSignal` as its last argument to cancel it in the core.

ts

```ts
export class Probe extends KeelObject {
  static create(core?: KeelCore): Promise<Probe>;
  counters(): Promise<ProbeCounters>;
  wait(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<number>;
  ticks(count: number): AsyncIterable<number>;     // backpressure through stream credit
}

export function add(a: number, b: number): Promise<number>;
```

Release an object with `close()` (idempotent) or with `using` where `Symbol.dispose` exists (Node 20+ and current browsers); a `FinalizationRegistry` is the backstop.

## Stores and signals

A store extends `KeelStore`. Every signal is a read-only `Signal<T>`: `get()` returns the current value, `peek()` reads without subscribing, and `subscribe(fn)` calls you on change and returns an unsubscribe function. Computed signals are written by the core.

ts

```ts
export class Todos extends KeelStore {
  readonly todos: Signal<Todo[]>;
  readonly filter: Signal<Filter>;
  readonly visible: Signal<Todo[]>;        // computed by the core
  readonly remaining: Signal<number>;      // computed by the core

  static create(core?: KeelCore): Promise<Todos>;
  setFilter(f: Filter): Promise<void>;
  add(title: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Todo>;
}
```

Change-sets are batched with `queueMicrotask` into one flush per macrotask, so several signals that changed in one transaction update together and a component never renders a half-applied state.

## React and the other frameworks

`@keel/runtime/react` exports two hooks. `useSignal` is `useSyncExternalStore` over a signal, with a server snapshot. `useKeel` creates a store when the component mounts and closes it when it unmounts; it returns `undefined` until the store exists, and `useSignal` accepts an undefined signal.

tsx

```tsx
import { useKeel, useSignal } from "@keel/runtime/react";

export function CounterView() {
  const counter = useKeel(Counter);            // undefined until created
  const count = useSignal(counter?.count);
  const parity = useSignal(counter?.parity);   // computed in the core, same change-set
  if (counter === undefined) return null;
  return <button onClick={() => void counter.increment()}>{count} ({parity})</button>;
}
```

Adapters ship for the other frameworks as thin files, exported from `@keel/runtime/vue` (`useSignal` as a `shallowRef`, `useKeel`), `/svelte` (`signalStore`, a `Readable`) and `/solid` (`useSignal` as an `Accessor`, `useKeel`). The frameworks are optional peer dependencies; the core package imports none of them.

## Query handles

A `#[keel::query]` becomes a store with five signals (`data`, `status`, `error`, `fetching`, `updatedAt`) plus `refetch()` and `invalidate()`.

ts

```ts
const inbox = await RemoteTodosQueryHandle.create("inbox");
const items = useSignal(inbox.data);        // RemoteTodo[] | null
const busy = useSignal(inbox.fetching);
await inbox.refetch();
```

See [Queries & mutations](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/queries.html).

## Ports

The ten standard ports and their types are exported from `@keel/runtime` and are not generated into your package. The browser defaults use `fetch`, IndexedDB, OPFS, `setTimeout`, `navigator.onLine` and `visibilitychange`; Node uses `fetch` and files. Replace one with `adapters` in `KeelCore.load`. A port you define yourself becomes an interface:

ts

```ts
export interface Http extends KeelPort {
  request(req: HttpRequest): Promise<HttpResponse>;
}
```

See [Ports & adapters](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/ports.html).

## Testing

The runtime is testable without a browser: over the `remote` transport against a native core, and against a WAT stub of the wasm ABI. The contract suite runs the same scenarios as the Swift and Kotlin runners, against the real wasm module.

---

Source: https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/roadmap/

Roadmap

# What is shipped, in flight and next.

Keel v1.0 shipped on 30 September 2026. This page follows the project's working record, [.10x/handoff.md](https://github.com/shreypdev/keel/blob/main/.10x/handoff.md), and changes with it. Last updated 30 Sep 2026.

Shipped

## v1.0

30 Sep 2026

The framework you can build on today.

- Records, enums, typed errors, objectsEvery public type comes from the schema and arrives in each language as that language would write it.
- Stores, signals, computeds, keyed listsReactive state in the core; list changes cross as O(change) patches.
- Ten ports with adapters and fakesHttp, Kv, SecureStore, Fs, Clock, Rng, Log, Timer, Connectivity and Lifecycle, with platform adapters and deterministic Rust fakes.
- Queries and mutationsStaleness, dedup, retry, optimistic rollback, an offline queue and persistence.
- Streams and cancellationStreams with backpressure; cancelling a call drops its future.
- Snapshot and restoreStores snapshot for crash recovery.
- Schema-hash gateChecked at load and at build; a mismatched UI and core refuse to talk.
- keel devA live core over a WebSocket, rebuilt on save.
- Teaching diagnosticsEvery macro error says what, why and how to fix it.
- 17 contract scenarios on 3 platformsThe same wire-level scenarios run against the real core on Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript: 51 of 51 pass.
- Adversarial reviews of every core crateSignals, runtime, macros and ffi were each reviewed by someone who did not write them.

Now

## v1.x

in flight

In flight for the v1.x releases.

- Distributionbrew, npm, a curl installer and cargo-from-git, each proved by a release dry run.
- Harsh-conditions benchmark suiteVery high-frequency data: firehose transactions, keyed-list churn, stream backpressure and a soak run, with CI budgets.
- Device-measured benchmark rowsThe same benchmarks on an iPhone, an Android phone and Chromium, replacing host proxies.
- A schema loader that survives dead-strippingSo the tooling sees the schema in debug and release builds without linker flags.
- Android keel dev remote modeThe Kotlin runtime gains the WebSocket transport the web and iOS already have.
- Dev-client auto-reconnectAfter a rebuild, a running app reconnects to keel dev on its own instead of needing a reload.
- WeakCtxLong-lived tasks stop pinning a runtime that was dropped.
- Macro diagnostic polishBetter wording for the query-in-impl and split-impl cases.
- Swift Port types publicCustom ports in Swift without the bindgen fallback.
- Full-JSON keel_schema_jsonSo the dlopen-based bindgen keeps doc comments.

Next

## v1.1 and v1.2

planned

Planned for the releases after v1.0. The order may change with what the benchmarks show.

- crates.io publishingPublish the crates under a registry-safe prefix; needs its own ADR for the renames.
- Frame-coalesced deliveryOnly if the stress suite shows the platform thread needs it. An ADR comes first.
- Maven Central for the Kotlin runtimeDepend on it from Gradle without a local build.
- Windows CLIRelease binaries and docs for the keel command on Windows.
- keel upgradeMove a project to a newer Keel version.
- Migration guidesFrom Kotlin Multiplatform and from UniFFI.
- A custom domainA home for the site and docs that is ours.

Later

## Horizon

exploring

Directions under consideration, not scheduled.

- Desktop targetsmacOS, Windows and Linux over the same C ABI.
- A first-party inspectorTime-travel over change-sets; the wire makes it natural.
- A sync engineA separate package, not part of the core.
- Compose Multiplatform interopUse a Keel core under a Compose Multiplatform UI.

Not planned

## Not planned

Shared UI of any kind, and hosted services. Keel owns everything under the pixels and leaves the screens to SwiftUI, Compose and React.

> ## How to influence the roadmap
>
> Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/shreypdev/keel/issues) and describe the problem you have rather than the feature you want; real projects and real numbers move items up. Anything that touches the wire, the runtime model, the threading model or a generated public shape needs a decision record first, and those live in [.10x/adrs](https://github.com/shreypdev/keel/tree/main/.10x/adrs).
>
> [Open an issue](https://github.com/shreypdev/keel/issues)
